159	## Writing UI code
160	
161	Rules for anyone, human or agent, adding or changing a JusPrin surface. They
162	exist because every value that is typed by hand drifts from Figma and from
163	the other side of the app within weeks; today's guards catch most of it, but
164	only if the code goes through the token file in the first place.
165	
166	1. **Never type a color, radius, font, or control size.** Every one comes
167	   from `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`. Native code reads it
168	   through `ShellTheme`: `palette(dark)` for color, `metrics()` for radii,
169	   spacing, and per-component sizes, `font(role)` for type. A stock
170	   `wxStaticText`, `wxTextCtrl`, or OrcaSlicer `Button` is
171	   dressed through `Shell/ShellRecipes.hpp`, never by calling its setters
172	   with literals. The Agent page uses only `var(--…)`: `--<group>-<name>` for
173	   color, `--radius-<name>`, `--font-<role>`, `--font-code`, and
174	   `--button-<recipe>-padding`.
175	2. **If the value you need has no token, add the token first.** Put it in
176	   the JSON, extend the guard in `tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp` so a
177	   later edit cannot silently move it, then read it from code. Do not write
178	   the number "for now": the guards cannot see a literal that is already
179	   there, and the next reader cannot tell a decision from an accident. A
180	   value that exists in Figma but not in the roles or scales is a design
181	   decision to raise, not a reason to type it.
182	3. **Layout spacing may stay literal, on the scale.** Padding between
183	   regions, gaps, and margins use 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, or 48 DIP.
184	   Control padding is not layout spacing; it comes from a button recipe.
185	4. **Pick the nearest role, never a bespoke size.** The roles are the whole
186	   type system. Bold at a body or label size is a role of its own; if a
187	   surface seems to need a size that no role has, see rule 2.
188	5. **Read the code on `jusprin-newui`, not old commit messages or Figma,
189	   when they disagree.** The header's chip and menu dimensions were once
190	   changed to match Figma and reverted because they looked worse; the
191	   token file records what stayed.
192	6. **Run the guards before calling UI work done:** `brand_tokens_tests`,
193	   `shell_theme_tests`, and `npm test` in `AgentUI`. Then look at the surface
194	   in the running app; the guards prove the code went through the tokens,
195	   not that the result looks right.
196	7. **Upstream files are off limits for style.** OrcaSlicer's own screens are
197	   retinted through the hooks `BrandPalette.cpp` installs and nothing else;
198	   see [Fork stewardship](fork-stewardship.md). Their radii and fonts stay
199	   OrcaSlicer's until the surface is replaced.
200	
201	## Runtime application in the native app
202	
203	The token file is applied to the running application in three layers. All
204	three read `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`; none of them carries a
205	color literal of its own, and the whole layer touches OrcaSlicer code in only
206	three small, additive seams plus one attachment point.
207	
208	1. **Fork-owned surfaces** (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/*`, the React Agent
209	   page) resolve every style through the token file, not only color.
210	   - Native: `ShellTheme` exposes `palette(dark)` for color, `metrics()` for
211	     the radius and spacing scales and the per-component sizes, `font(role)`
212	     for the type roles above. It is loaded once, by `Brand/BrandPalette.cpp`, and passed
213	     by reference into every shell widget. Widgets that paint themselves read
214	     it directly; a stock `wxStaticText`, `wxTextCtrl`, or OrcaSlicer `Button`
215	     is dressed through the three functions in `Shell/ShellRecipes.hpp`, so no
216	     fork-owned C++ file names an OrcaSlicer font preset or writes a radius as
217	     a number. `tests/jusprin/test_shell_theme.cpp` checks the parse and the
218	     fonts.
219	   - Web: `AgentUI/src/tokens.ts` writes the semantic colors as
220	     `--<group>-<name>` on every appearance change, and once at startup the
221	     radii as `--radius-<name>` and each type role as a complete `font`
222	     shorthand, `--font-<role>` in the UI face, plus `--font-code` for the one
223	     monospace role. The stylesheet may only say `var(--…)` for color, radius,
224	     and type; `AgentUI/src/styles.test.ts` reads the stylesheet from disk and
225	     fails on any literal, and on any spacing value off the scale.
226	   - Canvas: the Prepare canvas's tool strip (`Canvas/ViewportToolStrip`)
227	     paints with ImGui inside the GL frame, from the same `ShellTheme`. Its
228	     icons are the `currentColor` SVGs in `resources/jusprin/ui/icons`,
229	     rasterized white and tinted with the token colour. ImGui 1.83 has no
230	     shadow primitive, so `elevation.medium` is approximated with stacked
231	     translucent rounded rectangles.
232	2. **Retained OrcaSlicer surfaces** are retinted through the color tables
233	   OrcaSlicer already routes its colors through, installed once per appearance
234	   mode by `JusPrin/Brand/BrandPalette.cpp` from the end of
235	   `GUI_App::init_label_colours`:
236	   - `StateColor::SetColorOverrides` maps OrcaSlicer's brand and surface
237	     literals (teal family, grays, whites, text grays) to semantic tokens before
238	     OrcaSlicer's own dark-mode remap runs. Every widget built on `StateColor`
239	     switches at once.
240	   - `BitmapCache::SetColorReplaces` rewrites the teal in the SVG icon set to
241	     the action color at load time, and the monochrome brand mark to the text
242	     color.
243	   - The canvas selection is OrcaSlicer's own, unretinted: its silhouette
244	     outline, which OrcaSlicer ships switched off and the shell switches on
245	     while it is installed, plus its white corner brackets. The brackets were
246	     briefly given the primary action color; on the dark build plate that
247	     measured 1.29:1 in light mode against white's 9:1, and with the outline
248	     carrying the selection the override was dropped on 2026-09-21, which
249	     left `Selection` untouched by the fork again.
250	   - The ImGui panels, the canvas selection rectangle, and the About dialog
251	     are left alone in source: those surfaces are slated to be hidden or
252	     replaced, so editing them would be divergence with no lasting value.
253	   - The mapping table in `BrandPalette.cpp` is the reviewed teal-to-purple
254	     decision. Extend it there; never add a purple literal to an OrcaSlicer file.
255	   - Widgets that paint the teal without going through `StateColor` (hyperlinks,
256	     the settings tab underline, notification accents, Bambu-only dialogs) are
257	     deliberately left teal; the cost of editing them in busy upstream files
258	     outweighs surfaces JusPrin rarely or never shows.
259	3. **Identity** comes from two data-only mechanisms:
260	   - `resources/jusprin/overlay/images/` holds the splash, About and horizontal
261	     lockups, monochrome mark, wizard watermark, and window icons under
262	     OrcaSlicer's own asset names. `Slic3r::var()` checks that directory
263	     first, so no logo call site is edited. See the README there.
264	   - `Brand/brand_catalogs.py` builds `resources/i18n/<lang>/<app key>.mo`
265	     from upstream's `.po` files with the product name substituted, plus an
266	     English catalog for the source strings, so every language reads "JusPrin"
267	     without touching a string or macro in upstream code. Attribution strings
268	     in About are excluded by the script.
269	   - The generic printer profiles' plate texture,
270	     `resources/profiles/Custom/orcaslicer_bed_texture.svg`, is overwritten
271	     with the JusPrin lockup; the file name stays because five profiles
272	     reference it.
273	
274	`tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp` fails the build if a token edit breaks the
275	contrast rules above or leaves a token in one mode without its counterpart in
276	the other. The same test guards the radius, spacing, and type scales: the
277	`dimension.radius`, `dimension.space`, and `typography.roles` tables must match
278	the values in this document exactly, `typography.code` must stay a single
279	12/16 role, every component radius must be one of the scale values, and every
280	button recipe must name a type role rather than a raw size.
281	
282	Known gaps, all deliberate: ImGui panels and canvas notifications keep the
283	teal accent; the first-run setup wizard (an OrcaSlicer HTML page) is
284	Orca-branded until JusPrin's own onboarding replaces it; the About dialog
285	links to the OrcaSlicer website; vendor printer profiles other than the
286	generic ones keep their own plate textures; dark mode and the Preview canvas
287	were not visually verified.
288	
289	## Design handoff requirements
290	
291	Every high-fidelity product frame must:
292	
293	1. Define each application screen in one canonical appearance mode. Do not
294	   create paired light and dark screen frames. The other mode must be
295	   deterministically derived by the design system from the same semantic token
296	   names, component variants, geometry, content, and interaction state. Verify
297	   light/dark differences in the design-system primitives and semantic mappings
298	   rather than duplicating every application screen.
299	2. State the mode, viewport, component variants, keyboard focus, and any deliberate exception.
300	3. Use DIP, native density, and the standard radius scale.
301	4. Use HarmonyOS Sans SC for product UI, and monospace only for code (Figma's Code style uses Roboto Mono as a stand-in for the system font).
302	5. Show normal, hover, pressed, disabled, focus, error, warning, and success states as applicable.
303	6. Test long filenames, localized labels, dense settings, empty states, and narrow windows.
304	7. Use the original logo and existing functional icon system.
305	8. Label and justify any value that is not in the token files.
306	
307	The POC decks, rendered examples, horizontal lockup PNG, and generation sources remain available for visual-reference work through [POC reference](poc-reference.md). They are not runtime dependencies.

1	# OrcaSlicer integration guide
2	
3	**Status:** Canonical engineering guidance for the `jusprin-newui` production branch.
4	
5	This document records lessons from building and testing the JusPrin project-state
6	adapter and full-window UI against the real OrcaSlicer application. It is written
7	for future agents who need to extend JusPrin without having access to the original
8	spike sessions.
9	
10	The central architectural rule is that OrcaSlicer's C++ model, viewport, plate
11	list, and undo stack remain authoritative. JusPrin should expose those systems
12	through a narrow typed contract rather than copying project state or recreating
13	OrcaSlicer behavior.
14	
15	## 1. Source and scope
16	
17	These lessons began with two spikes on feature branch
18	`codex/orca-workspace-adapter-spike` and now include the full-window UI work on
19	branch `jusprin-v2-poc`:
20	
21	- Workspace-adapter implementation commit
22	  `4e278e3276a91a7142615492beb58bdf71116a78`.
23	- Invisible legacy UI implementation commit
24	  `65fc3b56e12e5be66851125cbedd8974d7eeb8c6`.
25	- Full-window UI coupling spike commit
26	  `462e243b46`.
27	- Canvas-wrapper rebase-risk refactor commit
28	  `bf7a0c1e10`.
29	
30	The detailed spike plans, results, evidence, and experimental code remain on `jusprin-v2-poc` at final POC commit `9bba835b92`. Use [POC reference](poc-reference.md) to locate them.
31	
32	The tested adapter surface includes workspace snapshots, object selection,
33	rename, duplicate, remove, undo, redo, change notifications, and committed
34	viewport transforms. The invisible legacy UI spike repeated the complete probe
35	workflow while an opaque empty window covered the still-mapped OrcaSlicer
36	`MainFrame`.
37	
38	## 2. OrcaSlicer-specific findings
39	
40	### Workspace changes do not have one event source
41	
42	OrcaSlicer reports selection, transforms, plate changes, content changes, and
43	history changes from different owners. There is no single event that means
44	"the workspace changed."
45	
46	The adapter must combine related native events into one logical notification.
47	The notification should identify which areas may have changed, and the consumer
48	should then request a fresh workspace snapshot.
49	
50	Do not place a copy of workspace state inside the notification. That creates a
51	second state-delivery path and increases the risk of stale data.
52	
53	Coalesce events at the logical command or transaction boundary, not after an
54	arbitrary event-loop delay. Union every reason produced by the transaction,
55	advance the revision before delivery, and guarantee that a snapshot read inside
56	the callback has the same revision as the event. Native callbacks may run before
57	the command that caused them returns, so ordering must be part of the contract
58	rather than an assumption made by consumers.
59	
60	### Undo and redo restore state without explaining the affected area
61	
62	OrcaSlicer's undo stack correctly restores the project, but a limited workspace
63	projection cannot always show what changed. A history step may affect settings
64	or other authoritative project data that the current contract does not expose.
65	
66	Judge history availability and command success from the authoritative history
67	position or an equally reliable owner-provided result. Do not infer success only
68	from UI button state or from differences in a partial workspace snapshot. Report
69	`History` together with conservative affected-area reasons so consumers refresh
70	from the source of truth.
71	
72	Do not implement a second history stack in JusPrin. OrcaSlicer must continue to
73	own snapshots, restoration order, selection restoration, and object identity.
74	
75	### The change log reads what OrcaSlicer already keeps
76	
77	The Agent panel's timeline rows come from a change log: one saved entry per
78	real edit, with a kind, OrcaSlicer's own raw name, an actor, and the
79	conversation item it follows. The local project store commits this semantic
80	log with the corresponding Orca model version. `OrcaWorkspaceAdapter` detects edits from state OrcaSlicer already
81	maintains, not from which code path ran, so a new OrcaSlicer feature that
82	records an undo step is covered with no fork code.
83	
84	- **Model edits are undo steps.** A step counts when OrcaSlicer's own
85	  `snapshot_modifies_project` accepts it (Action, GizmoAction, or
86	  ProjectSeparator, and a name not ending in "!"). The same rule drives the
87	  unsaved-changes asterisk and Orca's auto-backup while it is enabled. The
88	  managed JusPrin shell suspends that backup in favor of local versions.
89	  Selection steps and plate
90	  switching ("select partplate!") are excluded by it, and slicing never
91	  records a step. ProjectSeparator steps are project boundaries, not edits.
92	- **Every step reaches the adapter.** `take_snapshot` notifies with
93	  `ProjectStateChangeReason::UndoStep`. Before this, it notified with `None`,
94	  which the hub dropped unless undo availability changed, so a second rotation
95	  or a paint stroke reached no observer at all. `UndoStep` maps to no
96	  workspace reason: it never advances the revision or stales a queued action.
97	- **Detect by timestamp, not index.** Trimming drops old steps from the front.
98	  The uncaptured topmost placeholder (`is_topmost()`) carries the timestamp the
99	  next named step will reuse, so it is skipped and remembered as the first
100	  unreported timestamp. `Stack::clear()` restarts timestamps at zero, so the
101	  adapter resets its baseline at every project replacement (new, open, or
102	  in-place reset, which all publish `project_replaced`). When the active
103	  position moves without a new step, that is undo or redo, named by the first
104	  real step between the two positions.
105	- **Seven real edits have empty step names** (delete instances or parts, layer
106	  ranges, the printable and auto-drop toggles). The page shows a fixed
107	  fallback for them.
108	- **Settings are not in the undo history.** On a `Settings` notification the
109	  adapter re-reads the print, filament, and printer presets through the same
110	  `preset_deltas_of` the setup card uses, and reports each value in force that
111	  moved. A changed preset name is one switch, not a list of keys. Undo and redo
112	  restore configuration as part of the step already recorded, so during
113	  `inside_snapshot_capture()` the baseline follows without an entry.
114	- **Not recorded: edits that take no undo step.** Custom G-code from the
115	  slider, the plate settings dialog, filament mapping, brim ears, and the
116	  project cover image only mark the project dirty; plate rename does not even
117	  do that. The timeline mockup draws none of them, so no OrcaSlicer seam
118	  exists for them.
119	- **Edits are their own feed.** `IWorkspace::subscribe_edits` is separate from
120	  `WorkspaceChanged` so that recording an edit never changes the revision.
121	  The tool coordinator holds `IWorkspace::AgentEdit` while it executes, which
122	  is how an edit is attributed to the Agent rather than to the person.
123	
124	### Existing command paths are valuable and should be reused
125	
126	Duplicate, remove, transform, snapshot, undo, and redo behavior already exists
127	inside OrcaSlicer. Reusing those paths preserves worker cancellation, plate
128	membership, viewport updates, selection behavior, and history timing that would
129	be easy to miss in a new implementation.
130	
131	When a required operation is trapped inside presentation code, expose the
132	smallest behavior-oriented method from the current OrcaSlicer owner. Do not copy
133	the operation into the adapter and do not simulate clicks on hidden widgets.
134	
135	### Workspace IDs need explicit project-session scope
136	
137	OrcaSlicer's in-process IDs are useful raw identity, but the public contract must
138	not imply that they survive project replacement, reload, reset, serialization,
139	or application restart. Pair public IDs with an explicit project-session
140	identity and invalidate every prior-session ID when the authoritative project is
141	replaced.
142	
143	Resolve IDs against current authoritative state for every command. Do not retain
144	model pointers or GUI indexes across mutations. Keep invalid zero IDs, unknown
145	current-session IDs, and stale prior-session IDs distinguishable when callers can
146	recover differently from each case.
147	
148	### Presentation objects must not own model behavior
149	
150	A pane or list may render model state and refresh after a command, but its
151	construction or visibility must not be required for the command to work. Put
152	snapshots, model mutation, selection, plate membership, background processing,
153	dirty state, and event publication on one behavior path owned near the
154	authoritative Orca subsystem.
155	
156	Legacy presentation and JusPrin adapters should call that same path. Treat
157	presentation objects as optional observers, and avoid both copied handler logic
158	and simulated input against hidden controls.
159	
160	### GUI event-loop delay is not a project-ready signal
161	
162	The development probe can be constructed before command-line project loading
163	finishes. Even two delayed GUI callbacks may run before the requested project is
164	available, so the first probe snapshot can be empty. The invisible legacy UI
165	spike also observed a separate non-modal `Loading...` top-level during startup.
166	Its existence was another sign that window construction and event-loop turns do
167	not mean that project loading has completed.
168	
169	Tests must wait for a snapshot containing the expected loaded project before
170	starting commands. Tests that make visibility claims must also wait until
171	temporary startup windows have disappeared. Production code should attach to an
172	explicit project-ready signal rather than treating `CallAfter` as a readiness
173	guarantee.
174	
175	### History availability depends on which tab is on screen
176	
177	Some existing availability predicates combine undo-stack state with whether the
178	relevant panel is currently visible. That is valid for enabling a stock menu or
179	button, but it is not a project capability.
180	
181	Keep UI affordance predicates separate from model/history capability. A typed
182	workspace contract must read availability from the authoritative history owner
183	without requiring a tab, sidebar, or canvas to be shown.
184	
185	### Undo and redo can silently do nothing
186	
187	Availability and execution may follow different internal paths, so an operation
188	can still leave the history position unchanged. Compare the authoritative
189	history position before and after execution, or consume an equally reliable
190	owner-provided result. Report unchanged execution as failure and emit no false
191	state-change event.
192	
193	Do not use a partial workspace projection for this check. A real history move
194	may change authoritative project data that the projection does not yet expose.
195	
196	### A loaded object is not automatically printable
197	
198	Plate membership is positional: `PartPlateList` assigns instances to plates by
199	where their convex hull sits, and `load_files` on a bare mesh does not place
200	the object on any plate. An object can render, select, and transform correctly
201	while `PartPlate::has_printable_instances()` is false — and then `reslice()`
202	silently starts nothing ("background process in idle state" in the log).
203	
204	`PartPlate::add_instance(obj, instance, /*move_position=*/true)` is the
205	existing centering path (`PartPlateList::add_to_plate` uses it). Test fixtures
206	must place every object explicitly; the workspace and shell harness fixtures
207	do. A second trap: the plate's outside-instance set recomputes asynchronously,
208	so `has_printable_instances()` read immediately after placement can still
209	report the stale value. Judge printability from the slice result, not from a
210	check in the same event-loop turn as the placement.
211	
212	### OrcaSlicer has no printer object; a named printer is a user profile
213	
214	Upstream never loads `PhysicalPrinterCollection` (`load_printers` has no
215	caller), and its "Physical Printer" dialog is a Save-as: it asks for a name and
216	stores the print-host settings in a **user printer profile** that inherits the
217	system one. Two machines of one model are therefore two user profiles on the
218	same system parent, and a system profile alone is only a model. JusPrin's
219	`Printers/NamedPrinters` follows that: Add a printer installs and selects the
220	system profile, then `Tab::save_preset(name)` saves it as the printer, and Home
221	lists user printer profiles plus Bambu devices no printer stands for. The only
222	thing upstream does not store is which Bambu device a printer was added from;
223	that link lives in the app config section `jusprin_printer_devices`.
224	
225	Upstream has no rename. A rename is `Tab::save_preset(new)` on the selected
226	profile followed by deleting the old one, which is what a person does by hand.
227	An unselected profile is deleted the way `CreatePresetsDialog` does it (queue
228	the cloud deletion, then `PresetCollection::delete_preset`); the selected one
229	goes through `Tab::select_preset("", true)`, which selects its parent. A
230	profile with no parent is a custom printer, and `Tab::delete_preset` also
231	deletes the filament and process profiles made for it, so that case goes
232	through Orca's own confirmation. Names that differ only in case are one file on
233	Windows and macOS; never save one over the other and then delete the first.
234	
235	### Application teardown can re-enter destroyed owners
236	
237	Quitting while model volumes are loaded can crash:
238	`~GLCanvas3D → reset_volumes → Selection::clear → Plater::canvas3D()` runs
239	after `Plater::priv` is destroyed and dereferences null. This is inherited
240	upstream behavior — crash reports with the identical signature predate the
241	JusPrin shell (2026-08-28) and the stock-mode harness reproduces it with all
242	fork runtime code inert. Until it is fixed in upstream teardown ordering,
243	automated GUI scenarios should end on an empty project (`new_project`) before
244	exiting; both harnesses do.
245	
246	## 3. Resolved implementation problems
247	
248	### Selection events arrived before the duplicate command returned
249	
250	**Observed problem:** OrcaSlicer emitted selection callbacks while duplication
251	was still executing. The probe refreshed from those callbacks before it received
252	the newly created object's ID, so a later command could target the original
253	object.
254	
255	**Resolution:** The probe treats the command's returned `ObjectId` as the
256	preferred result and performs a fresh authoritative snapshot after the command
257	returns.
258	
259	**Lesson for future agents:** Do not assume that event callbacks occur after a
260	command returns. A synchronous native event may arrive from inside the command.
261	Use the command result to identify newly created resources, then confirm their
262	state through the authoritative snapshot.
263	
264	### Adapter selection needed exactly one notification
265	
266	**Observed risk:** Selecting an object through the adapter changes OrcaSlicer's
267	real viewport selection, which already causes OrcaSlicer to emit its normal
268	selection event. Publishing another adapter-owned selection event would produce
269	duplicates or a feedback loop.
270	
271	**Resolution:** The adapter changes OrcaSlicer's authoritative selection and
272	allows the existing canvas selection event to drive the workspace notification.
273	
274	**Lesson for future agents:** When a command already produces an authoritative
275	native event, observe that event. Do not create a parallel synthetic event for
276	the same state change.
277	
278	### Rename behavior was embedded in the object-list presentation
279	
280	**Observed problem:** `GUI_ObjectList` performed the rename snapshot, model-name
281	update, single-volume-name update, and mesh-name update itself. Copying that code
282	into the adapter would create two implementations with different behavior over
283	time.
284	
285	**Resolution:** One behavior-oriented command at the authoritative owner now
286	owns those steps, and both presentation and adapter paths call it.
287	
288	**Lesson for future agents:** Extract one shared command at the authoritative
289	owner. Presentation code and adapter code should call the same behavior rather
290	than maintaining separate copies. Any presentation refresh must be optional and
291	must not own the mutation.
292	
293	### Logical transactions are safer than delayed coalescing
294	
295	**Observed risk:** The POC delayed notifications until the next GUI event-loop
296	turn to merge related events. That made revision timing ambiguous and allowed the
297	adapter or consumer to disappear before queued work ran.
298	
299	**Resolution:** Coalesce low-level reasons inside a logical transaction and
300	deliver the committed revision at the transaction boundary. Use move-only RAII
301	subscriptions and dispatch state that tolerates unsubscribe or owner destruction
302	inside a callback.
303	
304	**Lesson for future agents:** Prefer an explicit commit boundary over a timer or
305	`CallAfter` used as a batching mechanism. If delayed work is genuinely required,
306	give every queued callback an explicit lifetime token; closing a window does not
307	make captured objects safe.
308	
309	### A parented top-level shell did not have an independent lifetime
310	
311	**Observed problem:** The first opaque shell was a top-level `wxFrame` parented
312	to the legacy OrcaSlicer frame. On macOS, destroying the probe also caused the
313	tracked legacy frame and shell to be destroyed. A parent relationship chosen for
314	window stacking had unintentionally coupled the windows' lifetimes.
315	
316	**Resolution:** The shell became an unparented top-level window. It explicitly
317	observes legacy move, size, visibility, activation, and destruction events, while
318	the probe remains owned by the shell. The final run destroyed the probe while
319	the application, legacy frame, and opaque shell remained alive.
320	
321	**Lesson for future agents:** Treat wx top-level parenting as lifecycle
322	ownership, not as a harmless z-order hint. Windows that must survive
323	independently should have independent ownership and explicit lifecycle
324	observation.
325	
326	### Native choice dismissal moved focus to the opaque shell
327	
328	**Observed problem:** Dismissing the native macOS `wxChoice` popup could leave
329	the opaque shell as the key window. The probe still existed, but it was no longer
330	the usable window above the shell.
331	
332	**Resolution:** The choice handler schedules probe `Raise()` and control
333	`SetFocus()` calls with `CallAfter`, after the native popup has completed its own
334	focus transition.
335	
336	**Lesson for future agents:** Focus after a native popup is asynchronous. Check
337	the settled state on the next event-loop turn, and restore the intended window
338	there instead of fighting the native control inside its event callback.
339	
340	### One-time window raising did not guarantee continued occlusion
341	
342	**Observed problem:** Raising the shell and probe once at startup was not enough.
343	Normal OrcaSlicer activation during project loading brought the legacy frame
344	forward, and OrcaSlicer also created a separate non-modal `Loading...` top-level
345	that was not part of `MainFrame`.
346	
347	**Resolution:** The shell observes legacy activation and geometry events, checks
348	coverage on a timer, and restores the order of legacy frame, shell, and probe
349	after ordinary non-modal activation. The spike also inventories shown
350	`wxTopLevelWindows`. An unexpected modal is logged as a test failure rather than
351	silently hidden.
352	
353	**Lesson for future agents:** Occlusion is a continuously maintained invariant,
354	not a one-time `Raise()` call. Covering `MainFrame` is insufficient because
355	OrcaSlicer may create other top-level progress, error, or modal windows.
356	
357	### Automatic top-level placement did not ensure visible placement
358	
359	**Observed problem:** The probe could be constructed, accessible, and reported
360	as active without appearing visibly above the shell on the tested multi-display
361	macOS arrangement.
362	
363	**Resolution:** The shell positions the probe explicitly inside its own screen
364	rectangle and repositions it when shell coverage changes.
365	
366	**Lesson for future agents:** Do not rely on operating-system placement for a
367	top-level tool that must remain visible relative to another top-level window.
368	Set and verify its screen position explicitly.
369	
370	### A borderless shell had no normal recovery action
371	
372	**Observed problem:** The borderless, no-taskbar shell had no close button, and
373	the normal Command-W shortcut did not close it. A failed development run could
374	therefore leave the legacy frame covered without an obvious recovery path.
375	
376	**Resolution:** The shell handles Escape and Command-W explicitly. Closing the
377	shell stops event tracking, hides and destroys only the shell, and raises the
378	already-existing legacy frame.
379	
380	**Lesson for future agents:** Every borderless development shell needs an
381	explicit, tested escape path. Recovery must reveal the existing application
382	state without depending on hidden controls or process termination.
383	
384	### Unsupported native selection could be mistaken for no selection
385	
386	**Observed problem:** The JusPrin contract currently represents object-level
387	selection, while OrcaSlicer also supports volumes, instances, parts, and mixed
388	selection.
389	
390	**Resolution:** The contract reports `Unsupported` separately from `None`.
391	
392	**Lesson for future agents:** When a new API supports only part of a native state
393	model, represent an untranslatable state explicitly. Returning an empty value
394	would give consumers incorrect information.
395	
396	### Invalid, missing, and stale IDs needed different errors
397	
398	**Observed problem:** A zero ID, an ID never present in the workspace, and an ID
399	for an object that was removed are different command failures.
400	
401	**Resolution:** Separate `PlateId` and `ObjectId` types prevent accidental
402	interchange. Commands reject the zero value as invalid, and the adapter remembers
403	which object IDs have previously appeared without caching editable object state.
404	Commands return explicit invalid, missing, or stale errors.
405	
406	**Lesson for future agents:** Define identifier lifetime and failure semantics at
407	the contract boundary. A generic Boolean failure hides information that future UI
408	and Agent consumers will need.
409	
410	### Sibling widgets and static owners must plan for destruction order
411	
412	**Observed problem:** The shell's status row binds handlers on the Notebook —
413	a sibling, not a parent — and the shell controller lives in a static slot
414	that outlives `MainFrame`. wx destroys sibling children in unspecified order,
415	so an `Unbind` in the row's destructor could run against an already-destroyed
416	Notebook, and the static controller's destructor could "restore" widgets that
417	no longer exist.
418	
419	**Resolution:** The row also binds the Notebook's `wxEVT_DESTROY` and skips
420	`Unbind` once the Notebook is gone. The controller binds the frame's
421	`wxEVT_DESTROY`, marks itself uninstalled, and abandons (rather than
422	restores) its canvas-presentation state, so nothing touches widgets during or
423	after frame teardown.
424	
425	**Lesson for future agents:** An event binding on any window you do not own
426	needs a destruction watcher before `Unbind` is safe, and an object that
427	outlives the widget tree must have an abandon path that forgets pointers
428	without touching them. Restoring state is for runtime detach; teardown only
429	ever abandons.
430	
431	### A canvas event posted from a command had not run when the command returned
432	
433	`GLCanvas3D::post_event` queues the event with `wxPostEvent`. A workspace command
434	that used it to add a plate, or to tell Orca a selection changed, returned with
435	the plate count and the object list unchanged, and the following read saw the
436	old state. Commands that must have taken effect when they return raise the event
437	on the canvas window with `ProcessEvent` (`raise_now` in `Workspace/OrcaOutline.cpp`).
438	
439	### `Plater::select_object` returns early when the canvas already holds the selection
440	
441	It skips `ObjectList::update_selections()`, so the object list can still be
442	pointing at the plate it last showed. The object list's own commands
443	(`toggle_printable_state`, `set_extruder_for_selected_items`, `fix_through_cgal`)
444	act on the list's selection and do nothing, without an error, when it is not an
445	object or a copy. Bring the list up to date first, and check the effect: a
446	command that can silently do nothing needs its result read back.
447	
448	### The object list changes the model without announcing it
449	
450	Switching an object's printable state or filament through the list publishes no
451	project-state change, so a view built on the workspace stays as it was. The
452	command that calls the list publishes a Contents change itself.
453	
454	### Orca gives every loaded object the first filament slot
455	
456	An object's config carries `extruder = 1` from the start. It is an assignment,
457	not a choice, so presence of the key says nothing about whether the person chose
458	it; the pane shows a filament only for a multi-material job or a slot other than
459	the first.
460	
461	### A plate carries settings only by Orca's own test
462	
463	`PartPlate::config()` has keys on every plate. The plate icon's "has plate
464	settings" test is bed type, print sequence, first-layer and other-layers
465	sequences, or a spiral-mode setting; the pane uses the same one.
466	
467	
468	## 4. Testing and verification lessons
469	
470	### Printer UI without a physical machine
471	
472	Bambu header-menu state, Select Machine, and print jobs are driven by the
473	in-process fake in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/`. Operators (humans and
474	agents) follow [Fake Bambu README](../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md):
475	JSON `jusprin.fake_printer`, a Bambu Lab system preset or a printer named on one, a scratch
476	`--datadir`, and the printer **menu** first row rather than the chip label.
477	Do not send keys or clicks to some other JusPrin already on the machine.
478	
479	### Run adapter workflows against the complete native application
480	
481	A fake workspace can verify contract behavior, revisions, merged reason flags,
482	and subscription lifetime. A fake cannot prove that OrcaSlicer's viewport,
483	sidebar, plates, workers, snapshots, and undo stack remain synchronized.
484	
485	Future changes to adapter commands must include both focused contract tests and a
486	native workflow against a deterministic multi-plate project.
487	
488	### Test the automation mechanism before relying on it
489	
490	The local computer-control backend could activate accessible controls but could
491	not send coordinate clicks or drags to OrcaSlicer's wx/OpenGL viewport.
492	
493	The required viewport selection and gizmo drag were completed manually while the
494	probe recorded the resulting events and snapshots.
495	
496	Future agents should test pointer automation at the beginning of a GUI task. If
497	the tool cannot reach a required control, switch to a documented manual check
498	instead of spending the entire verification window retrying equivalent pointer
499	techniques.
500	
501	### Accessibility state did not prove visual stacking
502	
503	The computer-control backend could inspect the probe's accessibility tree and
504	capture the individual probe window even when a full-display screenshot showed
505	that the probe was not visibly above the shell. Accessibility confirms that a
506	window exists and can expose controls; it does not prove what pixels the user
507	can currently see.
508	
509	Visibility and occlusion claims need both kinds of evidence: authoritative
510	window state and a display-level screenshot. For covering windows, also record
511	screen rectangles, focus changes, z-order recovery events, and unexpected
512	top-level windows.
513	
514	### Manual instructions must name visible controls
515	
516	An early instruction said "click Select" without explaining that `Select` was a
517	button in a separate window titled `JusPrin Workspace Adapter Probe`. Another
518	instruction referred to a menu path that did not exist.
519	
520	Reproduction steps must name the window title, visible control label, selected
521	object name, action order, and expected result. Internal class names and unstated
522	window context are not usable instructions for a human tester.
523	
524	### Isolate unrelated existing test failures
525	
526	The existing `libslic3r` suite contained one deterministic placeholder-parser
527	crash. The failing test also crashed when run alone, and the workspace adapter
528	did not modify the affected subsystem.
529	
530	The result was recorded as 115 of 116 tests passing. Independence from the spike
531	was labelled a strong inference rather than a proven before-and-after result.
532	
533	Future agents should rerun unexpected failures independently, inspect whether
534	the changed files can affect them, and report the evidence accurately. Do not
535	change unrelated code only to make the final test count green.
536	
537	### Verify state from callbacks, not from visual appearance alone
538	
539	The probe logs the notification revision and then reads an authoritative
540	snapshot from inside the callback. This proves that consumers see stable
541	post-operation state at the advertised revision or later.
542	
543	A highlighted model or changed list row is useful manual evidence, but it does
544	not replace checking the IDs, names, transforms, selection, and history flags in
545	the callback snapshot.
546	
547	### An assertion that expects success can score a defect as a pass
548	
549	The adapter self test asserted that `undo()` reports success. When `undo()` was
550	reporting success for an operation that changed nothing, that assertion passed
551	and recorded the defect as healthy. The bug was visible only as a contradiction
552	between two lines of the transcript: a command reporting success next to a state
553	check showing nothing had changed.
554	
555	Assert the contract, not just the happy path. For every command, check that the
556	reported result matches reality in both directions — success implies the
557	workspace changed, failure implies it did not. Such a check is never vacuous and
558	catches a lying result that an expect-success assertion rewards.
559	
560	### A check that cannot reach the code path is worse than no check
561	
562	The first version of that contract check passed while the defect was present,
563	because `can_undo()` was false, `undo()` refused early, and the buggy line was
564	never executed. It looked like coverage and was not.
565	
566	Before trusting a new check, confirm it fails when the defect is present. If it
567	passes both with and without the bug, it is measuring nothing.
568	
569	## 5. Rebase risk
570	
571	The rules for changing upstream-owned files — where to put a seam, when an
572	additive form is required, how to leave a resolvable conflict, and what evidence
573	a change must record — are in [fork stewardship](fork-stewardship.md). Apply that
574	document to every line this fork changes in an OrcaSlicer-owned file.
575	
576	Two OrcaSlicer-specific facts belong here rather than there.
577	
578	### Shared native state needs one owner
579	
580	Not every canvas-related control belongs to one `GLCanvas3D`. Orca's collapse
581	toolbar belongs to `Plater` and is shared by the Prepare and Preview canvases,
582	so two per-canvas guards cannot save and restore it correctly. Shared state needs
583	a single owner at the shared lifetime boundary: read and save the prior state,
584	change it once, restore the same value once. A setter without a corresponding
585	getter cannot provide exact restoration.
586	
587	This generalizes: a wrapper should own only state whose lifetime matches the
588	wrapper.
589	
590	### Churn is uneven inside a file as well as between files
591	
592	`Plater.cpp` is by far the busiest file this fork touches, but several of the
593	functions the fork hooks have not been changed upstream in the entire life of the
594	fork. Judge a seam by the history of the function it sits in, not only by the
595	file's overall rate. Name both endpoint commits whenever that history is quoted;
596	the numbers are not reproducible otherwise.
597	
598	The spike-era measurements, the wrapper refactor that produced these rules, and
599	the candidate refactorings that were never verified are preserved in the history
600	of this file and in [POC reference](poc-reference.md).
601	
602	## 6. Checklist for future project-state changes
603	
604	Before adding or changing a project-state adapter capability:
605	
606	- Identify the existing OrcaSlicer command owner, undo snapshot location, and
607	  native event source.
608	- Confirm whether the command calls `GUI_ObjectList`, `Sidebar`, `wxGetApp()`, or
609	  another presentation object anywhere in its complete call path.
610	- Reuse OrcaSlicer's model and history behavior instead of copying it.
611	- Keep OrcaSlicer and wx types out of the JusPrin-facing contract.
612	- Return explicit command errors rather than exceptions or generic false values.
613	- Treat IDs as session-scoped unless persistence is separately proven.
614	- Expect native callbacks to occur during a command, before the command returns.
615	- Use one authoritative event source for each change to avoid feedback loops.
616	- Merge noisy events, but protect every delayed callback against destruction.
617	- Give top-level windows with independent lifetimes independent ownership;
618	  observe their lifecycle explicitly instead of parenting them for z-order.
619	- Treat focus after native popups as asynchronous and verify the settled window
620	  on the next event-loop turn.
621	- Maintain covering-window geometry and z-order continuously, and inventory all
622	  shown top-level windows rather than assuming `MainFrame` is the only one.
623	- Position required auxiliary top-level windows explicitly and verify their
624	  placement on the tested display arrangement.
625	- Give every borderless development shell an explicit, tested recovery action.
626	- Report unsupported native state instead of silently translating it incorrectly.
627	- Wait for an explicit loaded-project condition before running a workflow.
628	- Run focused contract tests and the real native workflow.
629	- Use display-level screenshots for visibility claims; an accessibility tree or
630	  individual-window capture does not prove visual stacking.
631	- Use exact visible language in every manual test instruction.
632	- Separate verified behavior, inference, tooling limitations, and missing
633	  evidence in the final report.
634	- Prefer fork-owned RAII wrappers that restore exact prior native state.
635	- Give shared native state one wrapper owner at the shared lifetime boundary.
636	- Apply [fork stewardship](fork-stewardship.md) to every line changed in an
637	  OrcaSlicer-owned file, and record the rebase evidence it requires before
638	  calling the change finished.
639	
640	## 7. Known follow-up questions
641	
642	- Does the covering-window lifecycle behave consistently on Windows and Linux?
643	- Do movement, resizing, maximization, restoration, display changes, and multiple
644	  monitor arrangements preserve complete occlusion?
645	- How should a production shell present required legacy modal, error, and
646	  progress windows without exposing the rest of the legacy UI?
647	- What explicit OrcaSlicer event should replace event-loop delays as the
648	  production project-ready signal?
649	- Which additional workspace mutations need observation beyond the current
650	  select, rename, duplicate, remove, transform, undo, and redo surface?
651	- If the project later requires the legacy sidebar not to be constructed, which
652	  remaining `GUI_ObjectList` updates must be separated from model operations?
653	
654	Do not answer these questions from source inspection alone. Each question needs
655	a focused implementation or native runtime workflow with captured evidence.

1	# Designing an AI-Piloted OrcaSlicer
2	
3	## Executive summary
4	
5	An AI agent can remove much of a slicer’s technical complexity, but it cannot eliminate the need for user interaction.
6	
7	The boundary is:
8	
9	> The user tells the system what is physically true, what the object means, and what outcome is wanted. The agent chooses the technical printing strategy. The user verifies consequential decisions and remains in control of the physical machine.
10	
11	This produces three classes of OrcaSlicer features:
12	
13	1. **User-decision surfaces must remain prominent.**  
14	   These capture information the agent cannot reliably obtain: physical setup, functional intent, geometry meaning, aesthetic preferences, legal restrictions, and control over real-world actions.
15	
16	2. **Shared agent-and-user surfaces should be redesigned.**  
17	   The agent proposes a solution, explains it, and draws attention to uncertainty. The user reviews the result visually instead of manipulating dozens of parameters.
18	
19	3. **Implementation settings can disappear from the primary interface.**  
20	   The agent can usually manage line widths, speeds, infill mechanics, cooling, retraction, support parameters, and similar technical details.
21	
22	The final product should therefore retain nine primary surfaces:
23	
24	1. Project knowledge  
25	2. Physical setup  
26	3. Print intent  
27	4. Objects and plates  
28	5. Essential geometry editing  
29	6. Local meaning and overrides  
30	7. Print-plan verification  
31	8. Print preflight and live control  
32	9. Calibration and troubleshooting  
33	
34	These are not remnants of a legacy slicer. They are the information and control boundary between a person, an AI agent, and a physical manufacturing process.
35	
36	The interface should not give every retained feature equal weight. Features fall into four visibility levels:
37	
38	1. **Default** — continuously visible in an ordinary project.
39	2. **Contextual** — appears when the project, current selection, or agent uncertainty makes it relevant.
40	3. **On demand** — available through Project details, More, or the expert layer.
41	4. **Interruptive** — normally hidden, but made prominent when a consequential warning, mismatch, or unresolved decision occurs.
42	
43	Frequency alone does not determine visibility. A control can be rarely used but interruptive because overlooking it would be costly or unsafe.
44	
45	---
46	
47	# 1. Why an AI agent sometimes lacks enough information
48	
49	Before deciding which UI to retain, it helps to distinguish the different reasons an agent cannot safely make a decision.
50	
51	## 1.1 The agent cannot observe physical reality reliably
52	
53	A slicer may say that a particular nozzle, plate, or filament is selected, but that does not prove it is installed.
54	
55	Examples include:
56	
57	- The build plate was changed manually.
58	- The AMS contains a different spool than expected.
59	- Filament is wet, old, tangled, or nearly empty.
60	- A hardened nozzle was replaced with a standard nozzle.
61	- Glue was or was not applied.
62	- The print bed is occupied.
63	- A previous print remains attached to the plate.
64	
65	The agent can detect some of these conditions using printer sensors or a camera, but uncertainty must remain visible.
66	
67	## 1.2 The agent does not know what the geometry means
68	
69	A mesh contains shapes, not intentions.
70	
71	The agent may identify a hole, thin wall, flat face, or overhang, but it does not inherently know whether that feature is:
72	
73	- A precision bearing surface
74	- A screw hole
75	- A snap fit
76	- A decorative opening
77	- A sacrificial support
78	- A face that must remain smooth
79	- A surface hidden after assembly
80	- A region intended to flex
81	- A deliberately thin membrane
82	
83	This is why essential geometry editing and semantic annotation must remain.
84	
85	## 1.3 The agent does not know the user’s priorities
86	
87	There is rarely one objectively correct slicing strategy. A user may prioritize:
88	
89	- Appearance
90	- Strength
91	- Dimensional accuracy
92	- Speed
93	- Material savings
94	- Heat resistance
95	- Flexibility
96	- Watertightness
97	- Minimal support marks
98	- A particular color arrangement
99	
100	These priorities can conflict. The agent needs the user to define what “good” means.
101	
102	## 1.4 Some decisions are subjective
103	
104	Seam placement, surface texture, layer visibility, support scars, color boundaries, and acceptable print time are personal judgments.
105	
106	An agent can recommend an option, but it cannot determine the user’s taste from the model alone.
107	
108	## 1.5 Some actions have consequential real-world effects
109	
110	Starting a print consumes material, occupies a machine, creates heat and motion, and may run unattended for hours. Firmware updates and calibration changes can alter the behavior of the printer.
111	
112	The agent can prepare these actions, but the user needs final authority over them.
113	
114	## 1.6 Some information concerns ownership, law, or safety
115	
116	The agent cannot invent or silently change:
117	
118	- Authorship
119	- Licensing
120	- Commercial-use permission
121	- Safety warnings
122	- Assembly instructions
123	- Bill-of-materials information
124	- Intended use
125	- Privacy and cloud-connectivity preferences
126	
127	These are authoritative project facts, not slicing parameters.
128	
129	---
130	
131	# 2. The surfaces that must remain
132	
133	## 2.0 Project-window hierarchy
134	
135	The Project window should not treat Prepare, Preview, and Info as three equal destinations.
136	
137	- **Prepare is the dominant, persistent workspace.** It is where users inspect the model, communicate intent, manipulate geometry, resolve uncertainty, and review the agent's plan.
138	- **Preview becomes Check print.** It is a temporary sliced-verification mode, not an equal workspace. Leaving Check returns the user to Prepare.
139	- **Info becomes Project details.** It is a drawer opened from the project name or menu. The agent reads its contents continuously even when the drawer is closed.
140	- **Print opens Send preflight.** It never sends directly. Explicit Send remains the consequential commitment.
141	
142	The normal flow is:
143	
144	`Prepare -> Check print -> return to Prepare if correction is needed -> Print -> Send preflight -> explicit Send`
145	
146	### Default Project-window composition
147	
148	The default window should contain:
149	
150	- Project name and saved/unsaved state
151	- Compact printer pointer: target printer, nozzle, build plate, and material
152	- Compact, editable intent summary
153	- Compact active plate/object summary
154	- 3D Prepare canvas
155	- Essential direct-manipulation tools
156	- Compact pinned agent plan
157	- Highest unresolved assumption, compromise, or risk
158	- Check print
159	- Print
160	- Consequential warnings when applicable
161	
162	The canvas is the primary human-agent collaboration surface. It must make the build plate and model visible, support camera rotation, pan, zoom, selection, and direct spatial manipulation, and show the changes the agent makes.
163	
164	The compact summaries should keep the governing assumptions visible without expanding full editors. Examples:
165	
166	> Decorative · appearance first · protect front surface · under 5 hours
167	
168	> Plate 1 · Fuzzy Heart · 1 copy · PLA Matte
169	
170	A one-object project should not permanently display a large object tree. A complete intent questionnaire should not remain expanded after it has been answered.
171	
172	### Direct resolution of uncertainty
173	
174	Warnings should link to the user action that resolves them rather than expecting the user to translate them into legacy slicer controls:
175	
176	- `Support enters this hole` -> `Protect this opening`
177	- `Seam crosses a visible face` -> `Mark visible face`
178	- `Strength direction is unclear` -> `Show load direction`
179	- `Part may not fit` -> `Enter critical dimension`
180	- `Support may be hard to remove` -> `Adjust supports`
181	
182	Each feature still has one authoritative home, but summaries, warnings, and resolution actions may appear elsewhere. For example, Printer Configuration owns the installed hardware state while Prepare shows a compact pointer and any mismatch.
183	
184	## 2.1 Project knowledge
185	
186	This surface answers: **What is this project, and what does someone need to know about it?**
187	
188	OrcaSlicer exposes model descriptions, creator information, pictures, license information, profile notes, accessories, bills of materials, assembly guides, and other attachments.
189	
190	The project I inspected contained a safety instruction limiting it to electric tea lights. That information could affect how the agent evaluates material, temperature exposure, and intended use.
191	
192	### Why the agent cannot decide this alone
193	
194	The mesh does not contain reliable authorship, licensing, safety, assembly, or use-case information. An agent may extract clues, but it must not treat guesses as project facts.
195	
196	### What should remain
197	
198	- Project name and saved/unsaved state
199	- Project description
200	- Author and license
201	- Safety and usage instructions
202	- Reference pictures
203	- Assembly instructions
204	- Bill of materials and accessories
205	- Important profile notes
206	- Project save, version, backup, and ownership controls
207	
208	### What the agent should do
209	
210	The agent should read this material before planning the print, highlight contradictions, and ask about missing safety or assembly information when relevant.
211	
212	Only the project name and saved/unsaved state need to remain in the normal Project-window chrome. The rest belongs in the Project details drawer and surfaces automatically only when consequential:
213	
214	- Safety or usage warning: on import, when it affects planning, and before Print
215	- License restriction: when sharing, publishing, using commercially, or exporting
216	- Assembly instructions: for multi-part projects and plate organization
217	- Bill of materials or accessories: when non-printed components are required
218	- Reference image: when it clarifies orientation, color, or intended appearance
219	- Profile note: when the agent proposes deviating from it
220	- Recovery or version warning: when work is unsaved or versions conflict
221	
222	The user should not have to open Project details for its contents to influence the plan.
223	
224	---
225	
226	## 2.2 Physical printer setup
227	
228	This surface answers: **What hardware and material will actually perform the print?**
229	
230	### What should remain
231	
232	- Target printer
233	- Nozzle diameter and nozzle type
234	- Build-plate type
235	- Loaded filament and material
236	- Filament color
237	- AMS or multi-material slot mapping
238	- Printer availability and current condition
239	- Important mismatches between configuration and observed hardware
240	
241	### Why the agent cannot decide this alone
242	
243	Configured state and physical state can diverge. Selecting “PLA” in software does not establish that PLA is actually loaded, dry, correctly mapped, or compatible with the installed plate and nozzle.
244	
245	### What the agent should do
246	
247	- Discover printers and materials automatically
248	- Read AMS and printer state where available
249	- Compare observed state with the project
250	- Recommend compatible profiles
251	- Explain mismatches
252	- Ask the user only about unresolved physical facts
253	
254	The existing setup wizard’s enormous lists of printer and filament profiles should become hardware discovery followed by a short confirmation.
255	
256	---
257	
258	## 2.3 Print intent
259	
260	This surface answers: **What outcome does the user want?**

1	# macOS build troubleshooting
2	
3	Recipes for build failures on this fork that are environment/toolchain issues,
4	not code regressions. Kept separate from `agent-docs/jusprin/` because these
5	apply to the OrcaSlicer build system generally, not to JusPrin product code.
6	
7	## `liblibslic3r_gui.a` exceeds 4 GiB: Apple `ar`/`ranlib` assertion
8	
9	### Symptom
10	
11	`./build_release_macos.sh -s -x -b -c RelWithDebInfo` (or any RelWithDebInfo
12	build of the `slicer` target) fails while archiving, not compiling:
13	
14	```
15	[36/42] Linking CXX static library src/slic3r/RelWithDebInfo/liblibslic3r_gui.a
16	FAILED: [code=1] src/slic3r/RelWithDebInfo/liblibslic3r_gui.a
17	Assertion failed: (memberOffset < 0xFFFFFFFF), function update_block_invoke, file ArchiveWriter.cpp, line 276.
18	fatal error: .../usr/bin/ar: fatal error in .../usr/bin/ranlib
19	```
20	
21	All `.cpp`/`.mm` files for `libslic3r_gui` compiled fine; only the final
22	archive step fails.
23	
24	### Root cause
25	
26	Apple's stock `ar`/`ranlib` (from the Xcode toolchain) use 32-bit member
27	offsets internally and assert once an archive crosses 4 GiB
28	(`0xFFFFFFFF` bytes). `liblibslic3r_gui.a` in `RelWithDebInfo` carries full
29	debug info at `-O0` — the root `CMakeLists.txt` (around line 544-548)
30	deliberately rewrites `RelWithDebInfo` from `-O2` to `-O0` for easier
31	debugging — and as the JusPrin fork has added more GUI code (`Agent/`,
32	`PrinterSetup/`, `Home/`, `Mcp/`, `Shell/`, `Workspace/`, etc.), the archive
33	has grown past that limit. This first hit on `jusprin-newui` on 2026-09-13 at
34	commit `770bd2b0a2`; it will recur, and get worse, as the fork keeps growing.
35	It is not disk space (plenty was free) and not a code bug — the same source
36	links fine once a 64-bit-capable archiver is used.
37	
38	### Fix: use LLVM's `ar`/`ranlib` instead of Apple's
39	
40	LLVM's archiver (installed via `brew install llvm`, present at
41	`/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar` and `llvm-ranlib`) has no such limit and
42	accepted a 4,288,175,376-byte archive without complaint.
43	
44	**The trap:** `-DCMAKE_AR=...` on an *existing* build directory does nothing.
45	CMake only auto-detects the archiver once, the first time it determines the
46	C/C++ compiler, and bakes the result into
47	`build/arm64/CMakeFiles/<cmake-version>/CMakeCXXCompiler.cmake` (and the `C`
48	equivalent) as a literal `set(CMAKE_AR "...")`. That generated file also sets
49	`CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_ID_RUN 1`, and every later `cmake ..` reconfigure loads it
50	first and skips compiler/archiver detection entirely because that variable is
51	already set — so a `-DCMAKE_AR=` flag on a reconfigure is silently ignored.
52	(Verified 2026-09-13 by reading CMake 3.29's own
53	`CMakeDetermineCXXCompiler.cmake` and `CMakeCXXCompiler.cmake.in`.)
54	
55	To make the override take effect, CMake has to redo compiler detection from
56	scratch. Two ways to get there:
57	
58	**Option A — targeted reset (cheaper, not yet verified end-to-end).** Delete
59	just the compiler-detection cache files, then reconfigure:
60	
61	```bash
62	rm -rf build/arm64/CMakeFiles/3.29.0/CMakeCXXCompiler.cmake \
63	       build/arm64/CMakeFiles/3.29.0/CMakeCCompiler.cmake \
64	       build/arm64/CMakeFiles/3.29.0/CMakeDetermineCompilerABI_CXX.bin \
65	       build/arm64/CMakeFiles/3.29.0/CMakeDetermineCompilerABI_C.bin \
66	       build/arm64/CMakeFiles/3.29.0/CompilerIdC \
67	       build/arm64/CMakeFiles/3.29.0/CompilerIdCXX
68	cd build/arm64
69	cmake . -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
70	```
71	
72	`ar`/`ranlib` only matter for the final archive step, not for compiling each
73	`.cpp`, so this is expected to make Ninja only relink static-library targets
74	rather than recompile every translation unit — but this has not been proven
75	in practice. Adjust `3.29.0` to match your CMake version
76	(`build/arm64/CMakeFiles/` has the exact directory name).
77	
78	**Option B — full clean reconfigure (guaranteed, expensive; this is what was
79	actually run and verified on 2026-09-13).** Wipe the whole build directory —
80	it is pure generated output, safe to delete — and reconfigure from nothing:
81	
82	```bash
83	rm -rf build/arm64
84	mkdir -p build/arm64
85	cd build/arm64
86	cmake /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin \
87	  -G "Ninja Multi-Config" \
88	  -DORCA_TOOLS=ON \
89	  REDACTED \
90	  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 \
91	  -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=11.3 \
92	  -DCMAKE_IGNORE_PREFIX_PATH="/opt/local:/usr/local:/opt/homebrew" \
93	  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar \
94	  -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib \
95	  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local"
96	cmake --build . --config RelWithDebInfo --target all
97	```
98	
99	This pays for a full rebuild of the entire slicer target (every `.cpp`/`.mm`
100	file, not just `libslic3r_gui`) at `-O0` with full debug info, so budget real
101	time for it (order of an hour on Apple Silicon).
102	
103	**Deps-path gotcha, easy to miss:** on this machine, `JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local`
104	is an empty skeleton — no Boost, no TBB, nothing — kept that way to save
105	disk. The real, already-built dependencies for this fork
106	(Boost 1.84.0, TBB, OpenSSL, CURL, Freetype, libpng, NLopt, OpenVDB, GMP/MPFR,
107	OpenCV, JPEG, wxWidgets, etc.) live in the sibling checkout at
108	`~/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local`. A fresh
109	configure that only uses `build_release_macos.sh`'s own computed
110	`CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` (JusPrin's own deps dir) fails immediately with `Could
111	NOT find Boost`. Always include the OrcaSlicer sibling path too, as shown
112	above — this mirrors the worktree build pattern already used for
113	`jusprin-newui` worktrees.
114	
115	### Once fixed
116	
117	`build/arm64`'s CMake cache now has `llvm-ar`/`llvm-ranlib` and the correct
118	`CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` baked in, so ordinary incremental builds — including
119	`./build_release_macos.sh -s -x -b -c RelWithDebInfo` (`-b` = don't
120	reconfigure) — keep using them without any special handling. This is
121	deliberately *not* wired into `build_release_macos.sh` itself: the script has
122	no flag for a custom archiver or for the sibling deps path, so recreating
123	`build/arm64` from scratch again means repeating the manual `cmake` steps
124	above rather than just re-running the script.
125	
126	### Evidence
127	
128	Verified 2026-09-13 on `jusprin-newui` at `770bd2b0a2`: full clean rebuild via
129	Option B completed with exit code 0, zero `error:` lines in the build log,
130	final `liblibslic3r_gui.a` at 4,288,175,376 bytes (past the 4 GiB point that
131	broke Apple's `ar`), confirmed a valid `current ar archive` via `file`, and
132	`OrcaSlicer.app`'s binary linked successfully.

content.text:
**Verdict: the agent's description is accurate for about half of the committed docs, and those are the ones an agent reads most.** I read all 12 committed text files under `agent-docs/` (about 42,000 words). The rest are in ordinary, readable English, so the dense style is a writing habit, not something the subject forces.

## Where the style shows up

| Doc | How it reads |
|---|---|
| [mcp-tool-extension-guide.md](agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md) | Worst case, and a third of all the words. Edited in 52 commits. |
| [architecture.md](agent-docs/jusprin/architecture.md) | Dense, especially the newer sections on the plates pane and "Where logic goes". |
| [autosave-version-history.md](agent-docs/jusprin/autosave-version-history.md) | Dense throughout; reads like a contract. |
| [orca-integration-guide.md](agent-docs/jusprin/orca-integration-guide.md) | Mixed. The "Observed problem / Resolution / Lesson" sections are clear; the newer sections are clipped. |
| [design-system.md](agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md), [engineering-method.md](agent-docs/jusprin/engineering-method.md), [fork-stewardship.md](agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md) | Formal and rule-heavy, but in full sentences that explain themselves. |
| [product-definition.md](agent-docs/jusprin/product-definition.md), [macos-build-troubleshooting.md](agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md), [poc-reference.md](agent-docs/jusprin/poc-reference.md) | Plain English. |

[orca-feature-discovery.md](agent-docs/jusprin/orca-feature-discovery.md) is a near-copy of the product definition (18 lines differ), so it is plain too.

## The habits, with examples

| What the doc says | What a person would say |
|---|---|
| "The candidate catalog later in this guide is a map, not a licence." (tool guide, line 41) | The list of possible tools shows what we might build. Being on it doesn't mean a tool is approved. |
| "A description that has grown into a procedure is a skill that has not been split out." (tool guide, line 70) | If a tool's description has turned into step-by-step instructions, move those steps into a skill. |
| "It paints what two GUI-free models describe and sends each click to a workspace command." (architecture, line 97) | The pane draws data from two classes that don't depend on the GUI. Each click calls a workspace command. |
| "The unproven production delta is arbitrary semantic labels and their agent-facing representation." (architecture, line 154) | What we haven't proven is letting users attach any label to a region, and how the agent would see those labels. |

These match what the agent said about itself:

- **Nouns doing the work of clauses.** Words like "owner", "seam", "projection", "exposure", "delta" and "surface" are used as fixed terms and rarely explained.
- **Slogans in the form "X, not Y".** They sound precise but leave the reader to work out the meaning.
- **A spec or legal tone.** Long runs of "must", "never" and "do not".

## One thing the agent left out
